paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioGPT and Llama2, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing after applying various editing methods to BioGPT and Llama2, with "Base" representing the unedited language model. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³, with tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and ranges from 60 to 80, with tick marks every 5 units. Six methods are compared: Base (black circles, solid line), FT (blue downward triangles, solid line), IKE (red upward triangles, solid line), MEND (brown diamonds, solid line), MEMIT (purple circles, solid line), and ROME (green squares, solid line). All lines show an increasing trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases. The Base line starts at approximately 62% and ends at about 68%. FT starts at ~64% and ends at ~70%. IKE begins at ~66% and reaches ~72%. MEND starts at ~69% and ends at ~77%. MEMIT begins at ~68% and ends at ~75%. ROME shows the highest performance, starting at ~73% and rising to ~81%. All lines are smooth and monotonic, with no visible peaks or declines.
